rationale: No race telemetry exists yet (iteration 0, first draft), so this is a reasoned baseline rather than a tuned design. Speed: the course is about 4 to 5 m and must be covered in under 3 s, so average speed needs to be about 1.5 m/s or more. base_speed 1.3 gives a PWM base of about 2550 (62% of full), which should reach that pace with margin for slowdowns in bends, while leaving room to brake. Sensing: five sensors spaced 20 mm apart (x = -0.04 to +0.04) at y = 0.04, ahead of the axle so the robot sees the line before it reaches the wheels. The 12 mm footprint is smaller than the 25 mm tape, so the outer sensors read tape only when the line is near them, which gives a clear, roughly linear error signal. Weights -2, -1, 0, 1, 2 make the signal sign match the line side: a line to the left gives positive signal and steers left. Control: kp 2.5 gives a moderate turn gain (a full-scale signal of 2 yields about 1750 PWM of wheel differential). kd 0.3 damps the swing that a pure proportional law causes at speed. ki is 0 because the course has no steady bias to remove and the integral term risks windup on bends. line_loss 'last_direction' lets the robot recover toward the side it last saw the tape. Geometry: wheel_track 0.12 and wheel_radius 0.03 are mid-range; body_width 0.12 keeps the off-track limit comfortable (about 0.06 m or more); mass 0.8 kg with a 0.16 m body keeps yaw inertia moderate. Expected result: completion on the development tracks with a few line-loss events at most, small rms_error (around 0.02 to 0.04 m), and completion_time near 2.5 s. The main risk is overshoot on the slalom and s-bend, which the next race will show.
